tmu-micro2023-primary.title: A Tensor Marshaling Unit for Sparse Tensor Algebra on General-Purpose Processors
tmu-micro2023-primary.edition: MICRO2023 author version (title-page notice), institution-hosted; exact cached PDF
tmu-micro2023-primary.locator_basis: 1-based PDF pages (15-page institutional copy); figures/tables/sections verified locally; not handoff page approximations

tmu-traversal.statement: DnsFbrT uses constant begin/end/stride; RngFbrT uses parent stream begin/end plus constant offset/stride; IdxFbrT uses parent begin plus fixed size/offset/stride. ite produces induction indexes; mem loads p[x]; chained mem streams implement indirect lookup.
limitations: Table 1 names Index/IdxFbrT; nearby prose calls the SpMM primitive Indirect. This proposal follows the table signature. Integer signatures do not establish bit widths or legal numeric/address domains.

tmu-fig8.locator: PDF p6, Fig. 8 lines 2–21; §4.4; PDF p5 §4.2
tmu-fig8.statement: Fig8 traverses row pointers with DnsFbrT(0,num_rows), broadcasts row begin/end to two RngFbrT lanes with offsets 0/1 and stride 2, loads column indexes and nnz values, loads b through column indexes, LockStep-marshals paired vectors, and registers GITE ri and GEND re.
limitations: Two lanes are the illustration, not the Table 5 evaluated eight-lane system or a legal tuning interval. Boundaries require padding or an msk predicate (§4.2); Fig8 omits a concrete predicate/padding ABI.

tmu-cpu.locator: PDF p5 Fig. 4; PDF p6 Fig. 6 and §4.3
tmu-cpu.statement: TMU supplies required operands and ordered callback IDs. CPU ri multiplies vector operands and reduces/accumulates into sum; CPU re stores x[i++] and resets sum.
limitations: A CPU store is not a TMU scatter capability; CPU reduction is not TMU arithmetic.

tmu-tu.statement: TU fbeg waits for valid parent bounds; fite stalls on full circular streams, pushes iteration/control and stream elements; fend emits end. Streams within a TU are equal-size and controlled simultaneously. Element i of a child queue derives from element i of its parent.
limitations: Logical association does not define physical request/response tags or slots.

tmu-merges.statement: TG activity follows the preceding layer predicate; gite requires valid heads of all active lanes. Disjunctive merge consumes minimum-index active lanes and emits iteration, ending when all finish. Conjunctive merge consumes minimum-index lanes but emits iteration only when all active lanes match, ending when any active lane finishes. LockStep consumes active unfinished lanes and ends when all active lanes finish.
limitations: These general TG modes are context, not extra operations admitted for this Fig8 LockStep mapping. Sorted-coordinate merge preconditions are not discharged by retrieval.

tmu-outq.statement: Head/body/tail callbacks have IDs and scalar/vector/predicate operands. TG output FSMs serialize across groups with previous/next waiting states to preserve callback/operand order. outQ and its buffers are double-buffered; the core processes a full chunk while TMU fills another.
limitations: Callback order is not physical memory-response order or global CPU visibility. Ready/consumed acknowledgment, reuse and final partial chunk protocol are unspecified in inspected sections.

tmu-arbiter.statement: Cacheline requests prioritize leftmost outer-loop layers; select TUs round-robin within a layer; select streams in configuration order and requests within a queue in order.
limitations: No general CAM coalescer, duplicate suppression, predictor, response ordering, or fairness bound established.

tmu-sizing.statement: TUs of a layer instantiate equal stream counts and sizes at configuration. TUs within a lane share storage, allowing shorter leftward queues. Analytical queue allocation uses statically estimated nnzs per fiber.
limitations: Not a complete legal capacity/configuration domain or a proven sizing model for a new workload.

tmu-integration.statement: TMU traverses via coherent read-only requests from LLC and writes thread-private memory-mapped outQ into host private L2. It uses virtual addresses and host L2 TLB/MMU; page fault interrupts the core and MMU signals retry after translation. Context switching quiesces and saves/restores state including initial configuration, ite heads and control registers.
limitations: Paper assumes no shared read-write data between TMU/host/other cores. This route is not a universal CPU memory-consistency guarantee. Detailed drain/cancel/replay, fault ordering, concurrent source mutation and acknowledgment protocol remain unknown.

tmu-reference.locator: PDF p9, Table 5 and §6; PDF p9, §6 RTL implementation and area analysis
tmu-reference.statement: Evaluation reports gem5 v20.1.0.0, 8 lanes, 4 TGs with mergers, 2KB per-lane storage and 128 outstanding requests. Paper separately reports a SystemVerilog implementation and synthesis/place-and-route.
limitations: Reported model and RTL do not establish publicly accessible runnable source, RTL bytes, evaluated commit or an executable ABI. Reference counts are not supported tuning ranges.

tmu-scope.locator: PDF p6 Figs. 6/8 and §4.3; PDF pp8–9 §5.6
tmu-scope.statement: This proposed Fig8 mapping admits required operand/event reads only. Its CPU arithmetic, CPU stores and any atomic read-modify-write are outside the TMU operation contract.
limitations: Scope exclusion is a proposal decision, not a claim that every conceivable TMU extension is impossible.

tmu-unknowns.statement: Inspected primary sections do not establish concrete configuration/register encodings, numeric widths, physical response tags, chunk ownership/consumption/finalpartial protocol or complete fault/drain/replay ordering.
limitations: Evidence limit only; unknown is not unsupported.

mechanism_families.description: Dependent fiber traversal and ordered callback/operand supply; family confers no inherited capabilities.

designs.summary: Required operand and ordered row callback supply; host CPU performs arithmetic and output stores.

realization.description: Published Fig8 traversal/LockStep/output sequence supplies required CPU inputs and row callbacks; it is not one generic gather instruction.

result.form: Ordered callback-ID stream with paired nnz/vec operands for ri, and operand-free re row-end event.
result.validity: Valid active lane operands with padding or predicate treatment of exhausted lanes; stream association follows parent element ordinal.

ordering.scope: Mapped thread callback/operand sequence across TGs
ordering.description: Serialized outQ construction preserves callback order; no physical response or global memory order follows.

completion.event: GEND emits re after mapped row iterations. Full output chunks are processed by CPU; global done/consumed acknowledgment and final partial delivery are unknown.
completion.visibility: Paper-private outQ injected into host L2; CPU result-store visibility and universal observers are not established by this supply event.

requirements.description: Supply valid CSR ptrs of num_rows+1, monotone/in-range row intervals, aligned idxs/vals ordinals and b-contained column indexes; establish address arithmetic and accessible storage.
Provide CPU ri/re dispatch, initialized sum and row index, numerical policy and valid output x. CPU owns multiply/reduction/stores.
Establish padding or msk-based validity for odd-length rows, exhausted lanes and empty rows; preserve exactly one row-end callback even without row iterations.
Establish source/outQ lifetime, thread-private outQ and an alias/mutation discipline consistent with the paper assumptions; CPU outputs cannot invalidate source reads.
